attachments.origin_landmark: posterior surface and muscular process of one arytenoid cartilage (the laryngeal cartilages are not modeled as skeletal elements in this pass -- approximated via the adjacent hyoid attachment region)
attachments.insertion_landmark: corresponding points on the opposite arytenoid cartilage

actions: approximates the arytenoid cartilages, closing the posterior part of the rima glottidis

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The only UNPAIRED intrinsic laryngeal muscle: a single bundle bridging the two arytenoids. It closes the posterior intercartilaginous part of the glottis that the lateral cricoarytenoids cannot reach.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Percutaneous EMG-guided injection through the cricothyroid membrane (or a direct posterior approach), not ultrasound: with the neck extended, a needle is passed through the cricothyroid membrane in the midline (as for thyroarytenoid) but angled more posteriorly and superiorly, hugging the posterior laryngeal wall, to reach the interarytenoid muscle complex (transverse + oblique arytenoids together) between the two arytenoid cartilages; because the transverse and oblique fibres are intimately fused in the midline, they are targeted as a single unit rather than separately.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Posterior paraglottic/interarytenoid space, at the level of the arytenoid cartilages -- more posterior and superior than the thyroarytenoid target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG activity increasing with adduction/phonation; some series perform this injection under direct laryngoscopic visualization in the office rather than pure percutaneous EMG guidance, watching the needle indent the posterior commissure mucosa.
structures_at_risk: posterior cricoarytenoid, whose nerve branch (to the horizontal compartment) is closely connected to the interarytenoid nerve -- a reason transient breathiness/mild abductor weakness is a recognized side effect of interarytenoid injection
both lateral cricoarytenoid/thyroarytenoid complexes, which lie just anterolateral to the injection path
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The transverse and oblique arytenoids are injected together as the 'interarytenoid muscle' -- there is no technique in the literature that separately targets one from the other. Reported clinical uses include mixed/posterior-predominant spasmodic dysphonia and recalcitrant vocal process granuloma. Guidance is by EMG (or direct visualization), never ultrasound. No motor_endplate_zones entry is given: the available Sihler-staining study of this muscle maps nerve origins (bilateral recurrent + superior laryngeal nerve supply forming a dense anastomotic plexus) rather than a percent-along-a-reference-line position.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Fink DS, Achkar J, Franco RA, Song PC, 'Interarytenoid botulinum toxin injection for recalcitrant vocal process granuloma', Laryngoscope 123(12):3084-3087 (2013), doi:10.1002/lary.23915 (https://doi.org/10.1002/lary.23915) -- 8 patients, percutaneous office injection; Blitzer A, Brin MF, Stewart CF, 'Botulinum toxin management of spasmodic dysphonia (laryngeal dystonia): a 12-year experience in more than 900 patients', Laryngoscope 108(10):1435-1441 (1998), doi:10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003 (https://doi.org/10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003); Mu L, Sanders I, Wu BL, Biller HF, 'The intramuscular innervation of the human interarytenoid muscle', Laryngoscope 104(1 Pt 1):33-39 (1994), doi:10.1288/00005537-199401000-00008 (https://doi.org/10.1288/00005537-199401000-00008) -- 10 adult human larynges, Sihler staining -- all retrieved via PubMed
